Mathematically, it’s defined as the product of two circles (S\n1\n×S\n1\n). If you imagine four-dimensional Euclidean space (R\n4\n) as being composed of two independent two-dimensional planes, and you draw a circle of radius 1/\n2\n\t​\n\n in each, the resulting two-dimensional surface is the Clifford torus.\nHere is a bit more about where it comes from and how it’s used outside our framework:\nOrigins: It’s named after William Kingdon Clifford, a brilliant 19th-century mathematician and geometer.
